_doc: One entry per spoken line. tts = text the voice model reads (spelled for pronunciation); sub = subtitle shown on screen; shot = still in visuals/out; lt = show that member's lower-third name card.

lines.tts: Hello everyone, I'm Shagun from team Protocol X. Our project is a five-stage pipelined risk five processor, designed in Verilog.
lines.sub: Hello everyone, I'm Shagun from team ProtocolX. Our project is a five-stage pipelined RISC-V processor, designed in Verilog.

lines.tts: The problem we start from is simple: a basic processor finishes one instruction completely before it starts the next.
lines.sub: The problem we start from is simple: a basic processor finishes one instruction completely before it starts the next.

lines.tts: Most of its hardware sits idle while it waits, so throughput is low.
lines.sub: Most of its hardware sits idle while it waits, so throughput is low.

lines.tts: Instruction pipelining fixes this the same way an assembly line does, by overlapping work. It is the idea behind almost every modern CPU, so building one is the best way to understand it.
lines.sub: Instruction pipelining fixes this the way an assembly line does — by overlapping work. It is the idea behind almost every modern CPU.

lines.tts: Our objective is to design this pipeline for the R V thirty-two I instruction set, implement it as modular Verilog, and verify it through simulation.
lines.sub: Our objective: design this pipeline for the RV32I instruction set, implement it as modular Verilog, and verify it through simulation.

lines.tts: Hi, I'm Archit. I worked on the research side, the risk five specification and how pipelines are designed.
lines.sub: Hi, I'm Archit. I worked on the research side — the RISC-V specification and how pipelines are designed.

lines.tts: In sequential execution, each instruction goes through every step before the next one begins. Three instructions of five steps each take fifteen cycles.
lines.sub: In sequential execution, each instruction goes through every step before the next begins. Three instructions of five steps take 15 cycles.

lines.tts: Pipelining splits the processor into stages, so while one instruction executes, the next is being decoded and the one after that is being fetched.
lines.sub: Pipelining splits the processor into stages: while one instruction executes, the next is decoded and the one after is fetched.

lines.tts: The same three instructions now finish in seven cycles, and in the ideal case one instruction completes every cycle.
lines.sub: The same three instructions now finish in 7 cycles — ideally, one instruction completes every cycle.

lines.tts: We chose five stages because this is the classic risk design from Patterson and Hennessy. Each stage does one clear job, the stages are balanced, and it lets us study real problems like data and control hazards.
lines.sub: We chose five stages: the classic RISC design from Patterson & Hennessy — one clear job per stage, balanced, and it exposes real data and control hazards.

lines.tts: So an instruction flows: fetch, decode, execute, memory, and write back. Aditya will now take you through each stage.
lines.sub: So an instruction flows: fetch, decode, execute, memory, write back. Aditya will now take you through each stage.

lines.tts: Hi, I'm Aditya. I worked on pipeline design and verification.
lines.sub: Hi, I'm Aditya. I worked on pipeline design and verification.

lines.tts: In instruction fetch, the program counter addresses instruction memory, and the P C moves ahead by four.
lines.sub: Instruction Fetch: the program counter addresses instruction memory, and the PC moves ahead by four.

lines.tts: In instruction decode, the control unit decodes the opcode, the register file reads the two source registers, and the immediate generator sign-extends the immediate.
lines.sub: Instruction Decode: the control unit decodes the opcode, the register file reads two source registers, the immediate generator sign-extends.

lines.tts: In execute, the A L U performs the operation, and branch conditions and target addresses are resolved.
lines.sub: Execute: the ALU performs the operation, and branch conditions and target addresses are resolved.

lines.tts: In memory access, loads and stores read or write the data memory.
lines.sub: Memory Access: loads and stores read or write the data memory.

lines.tts: In write back, the result is written into the destination register.
lines.sub: Write Back: the result is written into the destination register.

lines.tts: Overlapping instructions creates hazards, so I built a hazard unit.
lines.sub: Overlapping instructions creates hazards, so I built a hazard unit.

lines.tts: When an instruction needs a result that is not written back yet, we forward it from the E X MEM or the MEM W B register.
lines.sub: When an instruction needs a result not yet written back, we forward it from the EX/MEM or MEM/WB register.

lines.tts: When a load is followed immediately by its use, we stall for one cycle. And when a branch is taken, we flush the two wrong-path instructions.
lines.sub: A load followed immediately by its use stalls for one cycle. A taken branch flushes the two wrong-path instructions.

lines.tts: Here is our test suite in Icarus Verilog: eight self-checking testbenches, from unit tests to full programs, and all fifty-one checks pass.
lines.sub: Our test suite in Icarus Verilog: eight self-checking testbenches, from unit tests to full programs — all 51 checks pass.

lines.tts: This is the real waveform of our B N E loop: forwarding in every iteration, and a flush on each taken branch.
lines.sub: The real waveform of our BNE loop: forwarding in every iteration, and a flush on each taken branch.

lines.tts: And here, the one-cycle stall after the load, then the flush for a taken B E Q.
lines.sub: And here: the one-cycle stall after the load, then the flush for a taken BEQ.

lines.tts: Hi, I'm Naveen, the project lead, and I wrote the core R T L. Let me show how the modules connect.
lines.sub: Hi, I'm Naveen, the project lead, and I wrote the core RTL. Let me show how the modules connect.

lines.tts: The program counter feeds instruction memory, and the fetched instruction is stored in the I F, I D pipeline register.
lines.sub: The program counter feeds instruction memory; the fetched instruction is stored in the IF/ID pipeline register.

lines.tts: In decode, the control unit generates control signals, the register file supplies operands, and the immediate generator extends constants, all captured in the I D, E X register.
lines.sub: In decode, the control unit generates control signals, the register file supplies operands, the immediate generator extends constants — into ID/EX.

lines.tts: The execution unit holds the A L U, the forwarding multiplexers and the branch logic, and its result goes to the E X MEM register.
lines.sub: The execution unit holds the ALU, the forwarding multiplexers and the branch logic; its result goes to EX/MEM.

lines.tts: Data memory is accessed next, and the MEM W B register carries the result to the write-back multiplexer, which writes into the register file.
lines.sub: Data memory is accessed next; MEM/WB carries the result to the write-back multiplexer, which writes the register file.

lines.tts: The four pipeline registers carry both data and control signals, so every instruction keeps its own control bits as it moves.
lines.sub: The four pipeline registers carry both data and control, so every instruction keeps its own control bits as it moves.

lines.tts: Each one supports stall and flush, and our top-level module wires all the modules together.
lines.sub: Each one supports stall and flush, and riscv_core wires all the modules together.

lines.tts: In phase one, the core, forwarding, stalls and flushes are implemented, verified in simulation, and the design synthesizes.
lines.sub: In Phase I, the core, forwarding, stalls and flushes are implemented, verified in simulation, and the design synthesizes.

lines.tts: On our test program, twenty-three instructions finish in thirty-eight cycles, a measured C P I of one point six five.
lines.sub: On our test program, 23 instructions finish in 38 cycles — a measured CPI of 1.65.

lines.tts: Our load alignment unit is tested but not yet integrated. That, larger benchmarks and F P G A timing are our next steps.
lines.sub: Our load alignment unit is tested but not yet integrated. That, larger benchmarks and FPGA timing are next.

lines.tts: Protocol X has built a working, simulation-verified, five-stage risk five pipeline. Thank you.
lines.sub: ProtocolX has built a working, simulation-verified five-stage RISC-V pipeline. Thank you.
